blocks.text: The hidden cost of poorly drafted SOWs

When your SOW is vague, you invite scope creep. It is not just about the extra hours you work for free. It is about the loss of focus on your actual billable work. Most consultants fail to define the 'Definition of Done' clearly. This makes acceptance a negotiation rather than a payment trigger. You end up chasing approvals for weeks.
Why SOW drafting becomes a bottleneck

The problem is often internal. You might call it a document review, but it is often permission theater. You lack the authority to commit to specific terms, so you wait for legal or finance teams. This turns a two-day task into a two-week ordeal. If you want to ship SOWs faster, you must define clear thresholds for what you can sign off on alone.
Fixes you can use right now

items: Create a 'Definition of Done' that acts as a payment gate. If the client does not respond within 5 days, the deliverable is deemed accepted.
Include a pre-agreed pricing mechanism for changes. This stops the endless debate on whether a request is 'in scope'.
Use an engagement charter for long projects. It keeps the focus on outcomes rather than just a static list of tasks.
Set clear authority thresholds. Know exactly what you can approve without waiting for a partner or legal review.

blocks.text: Lazur helps you draft your SOW text quickly. Hold fn and talk to dictate your draft directly into your document. If you are stuck on a clause, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to explain how to phrase a specific acceptance term. It helps you keep your language precise, professional, and firm.

You do not need complex software to manage these documents. Use tools that treat your SOW as data, not just a static PDF. Adobe Acrobat is standard for tracking. Specialized tools like GorillaWorks or SOWaudit can help you spot risks before you send the document to your client.

faq.question: How long should it take to draft a standard SOW?
faq.answer: Standard SOWs for existing clients should ship in 1 to 3 days. If it takes longer, your internal process is likely the bottleneck.

faq.question: Can I use AI to write my SOW?
faq.answer: Yes, AI can speed up drafting. However, always have a human review the final document, especially for high-value contracts.

faq.question: What is an acceptance gate?
faq.answer: An acceptance gate is a clause stating that a deliverable is considered approved if the client does not provide feedback by a specific deadline.

causes.title: Ambiguous language
causes.text: Using vague terms to stay flexible, which clients interpret in their favor.

causes.title: Lack of authority
causes.text: Waiting for layers of internal approval for every minor scope change.

causes.title: No payment gates
causes.text: Failing to define what happens if a client ignores a deliverable.

fixes.title: Define payment gates
fixes.text: State clearly that work is deemed accepted if no feedback is received within X days.

fixes.title: Standardize change orders
fixes.text: Use a formal, written process for every request that falls outside the initial scope.

fixes.title: Clarify authority
fixes.text: Establish concrete dollar or scope thresholds for what you can approve unilaterally.
